observations:
After reading the full source text of LM2 Torah 40 and examining all bechina edges in the dataset, the two packages identified (Chokhmah-Eyes-Tefillin and Melech-Tzaddik) cover all the explicit bechina relationships in the Torah.

The Torah's conceptual world organizes around two poles:
1. The wisdom/eyes/tefillin/mochin cluster — all aspects of divine intellectual illumination and its structural expression.
2. The king/tzaddik/hitpaarut cluster — the holy leader who is the living embodiment of God's glory among Israel.

The remaining major concepts in the Torah (Eretz Yisrael, Hashgacha, Nishmot Yisrael, Rosh Hashana/Kibbutz, Shefa Kefulah) are connected to these two packages through EITZA (cause-and-effect) relationships, not through additional independent bechina families:
- Eretz Yisrael's holiness IS a bechina of eyes (proposed addition to Package 1), but does not form an independent third package — it is the destination/result described by the eyes/wisdom family.
- Nishmot Yisrael draw out divine attention (Hashgacha) — this is eitza, not a new bechina cluster.
- Rosh Hashana and the kibbutz are the practical context/occasion for the tzaddik's Hitpaarut — eitza, not a new package.
- Shefa Kefulah (doubled abundance, para 13, Iyov 22:25) is introduced at the very end of the Torah and the text breaks off mid-sentence ('velo siyem'). There is insufficient bechina language in the fragment to establish it as a third independent domain. It appears to be a separate topic the Rebbe began but did not complete in this teaching.

Conclusion: The two packages account for all bechina-linked concept families in this Torah. No third independent domain with 3+ bechina-connected concepts exists in the source text.
